EDERAL REGISTE
VOLUME 13 NUMBER 80
Washington, Friday, April 23, 1948
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9950
Revoking E xecutive O rder N o. 9877 
of J uly 26, 1947, Prescribing the 
Functions of the A rmed F orces
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States, and as President of the 
United States and Commander in Chief 
of the Armed Forces of the United States, 
it is ordered that Executive Order No. 
9877 of July 26, 1947, prescribing the as­
signment^)! primary functions and re­
sponsibilities to the three armed services, 
be, and it is hereby, revoked.
Harry S. T ruman
The White H ouse,
April 21, 1948.
[F. R. Doc. 48-3673; Filed, Apr. 21, 1948;  
4:14 p. m.]
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9951
Restoring C ertain L and of the K uwili  
Park Military R eservation to the J u ­
risdiction of the T erritory of H awaii
WHEREAS by Executive Order No. 905, 
dated November 1,1940, of the Governor 
of the Territory of Hawaii, certain here­
inafter-described land in Honolulu, Ter­
ritory of Hawaii, was reserved for the use 
of the United States for military pur­
poses; and
WHEREAS such land is no loiiger 
needed by th^ United States for military 
purposes, and it is deemed advisable and 
in the public interest that it be restored 
to the use of the Territory O f Hawaii: 
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 91 of 
the act of April 30, 1900, 31 Stat. 159, as 
amended by section 7 of the act of May 
27, 1910, 36 Stat.. 447, it is ordered that 
the following-described parcel of land, 
together with all improvements located 
thereon, comprising a portion of the Gov­
ernment Land of Kuwili situate on the 
south side of Prison Road opposite Sum­
ner Street at Kuwili, Iwilei, Honolulu, 
Oahu, Territory of Hawaii, be, and it is 
hereby, restored to the jurisdiction of the 
Territory of Hawaii:
Beginning at the west corner of this par­
cel of land and on the south side of Prison  
Road, the coordinates of said point of begin­
ning referred to Government Survey tri­
angulation station “Kawa” being 163.20 feet  
south and 305.44 feet west, as shown on  
Government Survey Registered Map 2669, and  
running by azimuths measured clockwise  
from true south :
1. 241 °53' 55.00 feet along the south side  
of Prison Road;
2. 331°53' 98.57 feet along Kuwili Park and  
Playground (Executive Order No. 422 of  
July 23, 1930);
3. 50°33' 56.65 feet along Grant 8564 to  
Oahu Railway and Land Company;
4. 152°10' 109.70 feet along L. C. Award  
81 F. L. to Kahawaiolaa to the point of be­
ginning.
The area of this parcel is 5,755 square feet,  
more or less.
Harry S. T ruman
The W hite H ouse,
April 21, 1948.
[F. R. Doc. 48-3674; Filed, Apr. 21, 1948;
4:14 p. m.]
TITLE 6— AGRICULTURAL CREDIT
Chapter II— Production and Market­
ing Administration (Commodity  
Credit)
Part 245—Irish P otatoes
SUBPART— 1 9 4 8  PRICE SUPPORT PROGRAM
The United States Department of 
Agriculture will support the price of the 
1948 crop of Irish Potatoes at 90 percent 
of parity as of the beginning of the mar­
keting seasons through December 31, 
1948. Such price support will be accom­
plished by means of purchase and loan 
operations, of diversion operations to 
other than normal channels of trade in­
cluding livestock feed and industrial out­
lets, and of export operations. In most 
States purchase operations will termi­
nate generally in the early fall of 1948, 
the exact date possibly varying by States. 
With termination of purchase opera­
tions, price support will be effected by 
loans. Loans must be completed by De­
cember 31, 1948. Final dates for sub­
mission of applications for loans will be 
established by State PMA Committees. 
Loans will bear interest at the rate of 8 
percent per annum and will mature

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole paragraph orders that Executive Order No. 9877 of July 26, 1947 “be, and it is hereby, revoked”. Revocation is complete when the order takes effect, which is the signing date, April 21, 1948 (the filing stamp on the page also reads April 21, 1948). The command was exhausted by performance on that date; the end source is the order's own text. No earlier or later date is supported.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 9950 (13 FR 2191 (Federal Register of April 23, 1948)) was signed April 21, 1948. The filing stamp printed after the order reads April 21, 1948. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence ordering that Executive Order No. 9877 of July 26, 1947 “be, and it is hereby, revoked”. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on April 21, 1948. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. The only other held text containing this order's number is the Federal Register page of April 23, 1948 that reproduces this same order together with Executive Order 9951 (EO_9951.txt); it is the same instrument, not a later one. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9877 of July 26, 1947, which prescribed the functions of the armed forces remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists, because the only command in the order is the revocation itself and it was performed when the order took effect on April 21, 1948. The order states no effective date other than signing. The filing stamp printed after the order reads April 21, 1948. If the revocation were instead read as effective only on that filing, the date would be later than the date recorded here; the order text itself supplies no such rule. No later instrument is claimed as an end.","independent_command_check":"The only command is the revocation. The order creates no independent continuing duty, board, fund or authority that could outlast it; whatever the revoked instrument itself provided is outside this order and is not claimed here.","savings_check":"The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Order No. 9877 of July 26, 1947, which prescribed the functions of the armed forces stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked.","scope_check":"The held text has the operative inventory stated in the clause rows and no other command: no standstill, report, appointment, transfer or savings sentence."}

Section B. Clothing Allowance.
1. The amount of the cash clothing  
allowances prescribed in subsection Al  
(b) hereof shall be payable on date of  
first enlistment or first reporting for ac­
tive duty, and on date of reenlistment  
or recall to active duty subsequent to  
expiration of three months from date of  
last discharge or release from active duty,  
but shall not actually be paid prior to the
expiration of ninety days from and in­
cluding such date, or date of completion  
of recruit training, or date of advance­
ment to chief petty officer or assignment  
to band, whichever is earlier. In closing  
the accounts of a man discharged or re­
leased from active duty within the  
ninety-day period, credit shall be made  
only of an amount equal to the value of  
the clothing actually drawn, but in no  
case to exceed the total allowance pay­
able. ,
2. For the purposes of this order, an  
enlistment in any of the services men­
tioned in Section A subsequent to dis­
charge from any other of such services  
shall be considered a reenlistment. An  
allowance under subsection Al shall not  
be payable upon reenlistment within  
three months from date of last discharge,  
or upon recall to active duty within three  
months of last release therefrom, except  
as specified in subsections 5, 6 and 7 of  
this section. A man reenlisted or re­
called to active duty within three months  
of last discharge or release from active  
duty, who bn date of such discharge or  
release was checked undrawn clothing  
allowance in accordance with subsection  
P of this section, shall be entitled to  
credit for such undrawn clothing allow­
ance.
3. The allowance under subsection A2  
shall not be payable to—
(a) Enlisted men advanced in rating  
to chief petty officer while holding a tem­
porary appointment to warrant or com­
missioned rank.
(b> Cooks or stewards on advance­
ment to chief Gook or steward.
(c) Members of Navy, Naval Academy,  
or Coast Guard Academy Bands (band  
members) upon advancement in rating  
to chief petty officer.
4. An enlisted man reduced in rating  
from chief petty officer, cook, or steward  
shall not be required to refund payment  
previously made in accordance with sub­
section A2; and shall not be entitled to  
a second payment on subsequent ad-j  
vancement, or to a payment of quarterly  
maintenance allowance prior to the date  
specified in subsection Cl (a) hereof.
5. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A6 and A9 (b)  
hereof, upon subsequent transfer to,, or  
reenlistment within three months of last  
discharge in, another status which, in  
the case of first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a  
cash clothing allowance as prescribed in  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled to  
a credit of such cash clothing allowance  
without regard to issues in kind in the  
prior status, except that an enlisted man  
entitled to a clothing allowance under  
subsection A9 (b) on first reporting for  
active duty shall not be so entitled.
6. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A7 hereof,  
upon subsequent transfer to, or reenlist­
ment within three months of last dis­
charge in, another status which, in the  
case of a first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a
cash clothing allowance as prescribedjn  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled  
to a credit of such cash clothing allow­
ance without regard to issues in kind in  
the prior status..
7. Enlisted personnel described in sub­
section A9 (a), upon discharge from the  
Naval Reserve'(inactive) for the pur­
pose of enlisting in the Regular Navy or  
Coast Guard within three months from  
date of 'such discharge, shall, if reen­
listed in any of the applicable ratings,  
be entitled to a further cash allowance  
equal to the difference between the cash  
allowance payable under subsection Al  
(a) hereof, and the amount payable un­
der subsection A9 (a), and such enlisted  
personnel shall, if enlisted in other rat­
ings in the Regular Navy or Coast Guard, 
within three months from date of such  
discharge, be entitled to the cash allow­
ances prescribed in subsection Al (b)  
hereof.
Section C. Quarterly Maintenance Al­
lowance.
1. The quarterly maintenance allow­
ance prescribed in section A hereof shall  
be payable on the first day of each quar­
ter to:
(a) Enlisted men entitled to a cloth­
ing allowance under subsections 1, 2, 3,  
4, 5, or 10 of section A, or subsections B5  
and B7 hereof, or who were entitled to a  
clothing allowance under Executive Or­
der 9356 of June 24, 1943, as amended,  
commencing with the first day of the  
quarter following the first anniversary  
of the date on which they were last en­
titled to such clothing allowance.
(b) Enlisted men of the Navy and  
Coast Guard reenlisting within three  
months from date of last discharge, en­
listed men of the Reserve components  
transferred to the regular Service, and  
enlisted men of the Regular and Reserve  
components on active duty transferred  
to the Reserve or to the Retired List and  
retained on active duty or recalled to ac­
tive duty within three months of release  
therefrom, at the rate applicable prior  
to such discharge, transfer, retirement,  
or release, until entitled to a further  
clothing allowance.
2. Enlisted men of the Naval Reserve  
undergoing training leading to a com­
mission, enlisted men of the Naval Re­
serve (inactive) and enlisted men hold­
ing temporary appointments to warrant  
or Commissioned rank shall not be en­
titled to quarterly maintenance allow­
ances. Enlisted men entitled to a  
clothing allowance on the first day of  
the quarter shall not be entitled to any  
quarterly maintenance allowance other­
wise due them on that date.
This order shall supersede Executive  
Orders No. 9744B of June 29, 1946, No.  
9785 of October 1, 1946, and No. 9869 of  
June 30, 1947, and shall be effective £ ls  
of July 1, 1948, and continue in effect  
for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949.

Section B. Clothing Allowance.
1. The amount of the cash clothing  
allowances prescribed in subsection Al  
(b) hereof shall be payable on date of  
first enlistment or first reporting for ac­
tive duty, and on date of reenlistment  
or recall to active duty subsequent to  
expiration of three months from date of  
last discharge or release from active duty,  
but shall not actually be paid prior to the
expiration of ninety days from and in­
cluding such date, or date of completion  
of recruit training, or date of advance­
ment to chief petty officer or assignment  
to band, whichever is earlier. In closing  
the accounts of a man discharged or re­
leased from active duty within the  
ninety-day period, credit shall be made  
only of an amount equal to the value of  
the clothing actually drawn, but in no  
case to exceed the total allowance pay­
able. ,
2. For the purposes of this order, an  
enlistment in any of the services men­
tioned in Section A subsequent to dis­
charge from any other of such services  
shall be considered a reenlistment. An  
allowance under subsection Al shall not  
be payable upon reenlistment within  
three months from date of last discharge,  
or upon recall to active duty within three  
months of last release therefrom, except  
as specified in subsections 5, 6 and 7 of  
this section. A man reenlisted or re­
called to active duty within three months  
of last discharge or release from active  
duty, who bn date of such discharge or  
release was checked undrawn clothing  
allowance in accordance with subsection  
P of this section, shall be entitled to  
credit for such undrawn clothing allow­
ance.
3. The allowance under subsection A2  
shall not be payable to—
(a) Enlisted men advanced in rating  
to chief petty officer while holding a tem­
porary appointment to warrant or com­
missioned rank.
(b> Cooks or stewards on advance­
ment to chief Gook or steward.
(c) Members of Navy, Naval Academy,  
or Coast Guard Academy Bands (band  
members) upon advancement in rating  
to chief petty officer.
4. An enlisted man reduced in rating  
from chief petty officer, cook, or steward  
shall not be required to refund payment  
previously made in accordance with sub­
section A2; and shall not be entitled to  
a second payment on subsequent ad-j  
vancement, or to a payment of quarterly  
maintenance allowance prior to the date  
specified in subsection Cl (a) hereof.
5. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A6 and A9 (b)  
hereof, upon subsequent transfer to,, or  
reenlistment within three months of last  
discharge in, another status which, in  
the case of first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a  
cash clothing allowance as prescribed in  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled to  
a credit of such cash clothing allowance  
without regard to issues in kind in the  
prior status, except that an enlisted man  
entitled to a clothing allowance under  
subsection A9 (b) on first reporting for  
active duty shall not be so entitled.
6. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A7 hereof,  
upon subsequent transfer to, or reenlist­
ment within three months of last dis­
charge in, another status which, in the  
case of a first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a
cash clothing allowance as prescribedjn  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled  
to a credit of such cash clothing allow­
ance without regard to issues in kind in  
the prior status..
7. Enlisted personnel described in sub­
section A9 (a), upon discharge from the  
Naval Reserve'(inactive) for the pur­
pose of enlisting in the Regular Navy or  
Coast Guard within three months from  
date of 'such discharge, shall, if reen­
listed in any of the applicable ratings,  
be entitled to a further cash allowance  
equal to the difference between the cash  
allowance payable under subsection Al  
(a) hereof, and the amount payable un­
der subsection A9 (a), and such enlisted  
personnel shall, if enlisted in other rat­
ings in the Regular Navy or Coast Guard, 
within three months from date of such  
discharge, be entitled to the cash allow­
ances prescribed in subsection Al (b)  
hereof.
Section C. Quarterly Maintenance Al­
lowance.
1. The quarterly maintenance allow­
ance prescribed in section A hereof shall  
be payable on the first day of each quar­
ter to:
(a) Enlisted men entitled to a cloth­
ing allowance under subsections 1, 2, 3,  
4, 5, or 10 of section A, or subsections B5  
and B7 hereof, or who were entitled to a  
clothing allowance under Executive Or­
der 9356 of June 24, 1943, as amended,  
commencing with the first day of the  
quarter following the first anniversary  
of the date on which they were last en­
titled to such clothing allowance.
(b) Enlisted men of the Navy and  
Coast Guard reenlisting within three  
months from date of last discharge, en­
listed men of the Reserve components  
transferred to the regular Service, and  
enlisted men of the Regular and Reserve  
components on active duty transferred  
to the Reserve or to the Retired List and  
retained on active duty or recalled to ac­
tive duty within three months of release  
therefrom, at the rate applicable prior  
to such discharge, transfer, retirement,  
or release, until entitled to a further  
clothing allowance.
2. Enlisted men of the Naval Reserve  
undergoing training leading to a com­
mission, enlisted men of the Naval Re­
serve (inactive) and enlisted men hold­
ing temporary appointments to warrant  
or Commissioned rank shall not be en­
titled to quarterly maintenance allow­
ances. Enlisted men entitled to a  
clothing allowance on the first day of  
the quarter shall not be entitled to any  
quarterly maintenance allowance other­
wise due them on that date.
This order shall supersede Executive  
Orders No. 9744B of June 29, 1946, No.  
9785 of October 1, 1946, and No. 9869 of  
June 30, 1947, and shall be effective £ ls  
of July 1, 1948, and continue in effect  
for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Section A lists the clothing in kind or cash allowances to which enlisted men are entitled, in tables that the OCR text breaks into fragments. It continues until the closing paragraph's sunset on June 30, 1949. Executive Order 10023, signed December 20, 1948 and effective as of December 1, 1948, adds a new subsection 11 to Section A (a cash allowance not to exceed $80.00 for the full dress uniform) for members of the United States Navy Band; under the owner ruling on amendments this is a later event and the clause continues, amended, until the order ends.

Section B. Clothing Allowance.
1. The amount of the cash clothing  
allowances prescribed in subsection Al  
(b) hereof shall be payable on date of  
first enlistment or first reporting for ac­
tive duty, and on date of reenlistment  
or recall to active duty subsequent to  
expiration of three months from date of  
last discharge or release from active duty,  
but shall not actually be paid prior to the
expiration of ninety days from and in­
cluding such date, or date of completion  
of recruit training, or date of advance­
ment to chief petty officer or assignment  
to band, whichever is earlier. In closing  
the accounts of a man discharged or re­
leased from active duty within the  
ninety-day period, credit shall be made  
only of an amount equal to the value of  
the clothing actually drawn, but in no  
case to exceed the total allowance pay­
able. ,
2. For the purposes of this order, an  
enlistment in any of the services men­
tioned in Section A subsequent to dis­
charge from any other of such services  
shall be considered a reenlistment. An  
allowance under subsection Al shall not  
be payable upon reenlistment within  
three months from date of last discharge,  
or upon recall to active duty within three  
months of last release therefrom, except  
as specified in subsections 5, 6 and 7 of  
this section. A man reenlisted or re­
called to active duty within three months  
of last discharge or release from active  
duty, who bn date of such discharge or  
release was checked undrawn clothing  
allowance in accordance with subsection  
P of this section, shall be entitled to  
credit for such undrawn clothing allow­
ance.
3. The allowance under subsection A2  
shall not be payable to—
(a) Enlisted men advanced in rating  
to chief petty officer while holding a tem­
porary appointment to warrant or com­
missioned rank.
(b> Cooks or stewards on advance­
ment to chief Gook or steward.
(c) Members of Navy, Naval Academy,  
or Coast Guard Academy Bands (band  
members) upon advancement in rating  
to chief petty officer.
4. An enlisted man reduced in rating  
from chief petty officer, cook, or steward  
shall not be required to refund payment  
previously made in accordance with sub­
section A2; and shall not be entitled to  
a second payment on subsequent ad-j  
vancement, or to a payment of quarterly  
maintenance allowance prior to the date  
specified in subsection Cl (a) hereof.
5. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A6 and A9 (b)  
hereof, upon subsequent transfer to,, or  
reenlistment within three months of last  
discharge in, another status which, in  
the case of first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a  
cash clothing allowance as prescribed in  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled to  
a credit of such cash clothing allowance  
without regard to issues in kind in the  
prior status, except that an enlisted man  
entitled to a clothing allowance under  
subsection A9 (b) on first reporting for  
active duty shall not be so entitled.
6. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A7 hereof,  
upon subsequent transfer to, or reenlist­
ment within three months of last dis­
charge in, another status which, in the  
case of a first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a
cash clothing allowance as prescribedjn  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled  
to a credit of such cash clothing allow­
ance without regard to issues in kind in  
the prior status..
7. Enlisted personnel described in sub­
section A9 (a), upon discharge from the  
Naval Reserve'(inactive) for the pur­
pose of enlisting in the Regular Navy or  
Coast Guard within three months from  
date of 'such discharge, shall, if reen­
listed in any of the applicable ratings,  
be entitled to a further cash allowance  
equal to the difference between the cash  
allowance payable under subsection Al  
(a) hereof, and the amount payable un­
der subsection A9 (a), and such enlisted  
personnel shall, if enlisted in other rat­
ings in the Regular Navy or Coast Guard, 
within three months from date of such  
discharge, be entitled to the cash allow­
ances prescribed in subsection Al (b)  
hereof.
Section C. Quarterly Maintenance Al­
lowance.
1. The quarterly maintenance allow­
ance prescribed in section A hereof shall  
be payable on the first day of each quar­
ter to:
(a) Enlisted men entitled to a cloth­
ing allowance under subsections 1, 2, 3,  
4, 5, or 10 of section A, or subsections B5  
and B7 hereof, or who were entitled to a  
clothing allowance under Executive Or­
der 9356 of June 24, 1943, as amended,  
commencing with the first day of the  
quarter following the first anniversary  
of the date on which they were last en­
titled to such clothing allowance.
(b) Enlisted men of the Navy and  
Coast Guard reenlisting within three  
months from date of last discharge, en­
listed men of the Reserve components  
transferred to the regular Service, and  
enlisted men of the Regular and Reserve  
components on active duty transferred  
to the Reserve or to the Retired List and  
retained on active duty or recalled to ac­
tive duty within three months of release  
therefrom, at the rate applicable prior  
to such discharge, transfer, retirement,  
or release, until entitled to a further  
clothing allowance.
2. Enlisted men of the Naval Reserve  
undergoing training leading to a com­
mission, enlisted men of the Naval Re­
serve (inactive) and enlisted men hold­
ing temporary appointments to warrant  
or Commissioned rank shall not be en­
titled to quarterly maintenance allow­
ances. Enlisted men entitled to a  
clothing allowance on the first day of  
the quarter shall not be entitled to any  
quarterly maintenance allowance other­
wise due them on that date.

Orders No. 9744B of June 29, 1946, No.

for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949.

Section B. Clothing Allowance.
1. The amount of the cash clothing  
allowances prescribed in subsection Al  
(b) hereof shall be payable on date of  
first enlistment or first reporting for ac­
tive duty, and on date of reenlistment  
or recall to active duty subsequent to  
expiration of three months from date of  
last discharge or release from active duty,  
but shall not actually be paid prior to the
expiration of ninety days from and in­
cluding such date, or date of completion  
of recruit training, or date of advance­
ment to chief petty officer or assignment  
to band, whichever is earlier. In closing  
the accounts of a man discharged or re­
leased from active duty within the  
ninety-day period, credit shall be made  
only of an amount equal to the value of  
the clothing actually drawn, but in no  
case to exceed the total allowance pay­
able. ,
2. For the purposes of this order, an  
enlistment in any of the services men­
tioned in Section A subsequent to dis­
charge from any other of such services  
shall be considered a reenlistment. An  
allowance under subsection Al shall not  
be payable upon reenlistment within  
three months from date of last discharge,  
or upon recall to active duty within three  
months of last release therefrom, except  
as specified in subsections 5, 6 and 7 of  
this section. A man reenlisted or re­
called to active duty within three months  
of last discharge or release from active  
duty, who bn date of such discharge or  
release was checked undrawn clothing  
allowance in accordance with subsection  
P of this section, shall be entitled to  
credit for such undrawn clothing allow­
ance.
3. The allowance under subsection A2  
shall not be payable to—
(a) Enlisted men advanced in rating  
to chief petty officer while holding a tem­
porary appointment to warrant or com­
missioned rank.
(b> Cooks or stewards on advance­
ment to chief Gook or steward.
(c) Members of Navy, Naval Academy,  
or Coast Guard Academy Bands (band  
members) upon advancement in rating  
to chief petty officer.
4. An enlisted man reduced in rating  
from chief petty officer, cook, or steward  
shall not be required to refund payment  
previously made in accordance with sub­
section A2; and shall not be entitled to  
a second payment on subsequent ad-j  
vancement, or to a payment of quarterly  
maintenance allowance prior to the date  
specified in subsection Cl (a) hereof.
5. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A6 and A9 (b)  
hereof, upon subsequent transfer to,, or  
reenlistment within three months of last  
discharge in, another status which, in  
the case of first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a  
cash clothing allowance as prescribed in  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled to  
a credit of such cash clothing allowance  
without regard to issues in kind in the  
prior status, except that an enlisted man  
entitled to a clothing allowance under  
subsection A9 (b) on first reporting for  
active duty shall not be so entitled.
6. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A7 hereof,  
upon subsequent transfer to, or reenlist­
ment within three months of last dis­
charge in, another status which, in the  
case of a first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a
cash clothing allowance as prescribedjn  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled  
to a credit of such cash clothing allow­
ance without regard to issues in kind in  
the prior status..
7. Enlisted personnel described in sub­
section A9 (a), upon discharge from the  
Naval Reserve'(inactive) for the pur­
pose of enlisting in the Regular Navy or  
Coast Guard within three months from  
date of 'such discharge, shall, if reen­
listed in any of the applicable ratings,  
be entitled to a further cash allowance  
equal to the difference between the cash  
allowance payable under subsection Al  
(a) hereof, and the amount payable un­
der subsection A9 (a), and such enlisted  
personnel shall, if enlisted in other rat­
ings in the Regular Navy or Coast Guard, 
within three months from date of such  
discharge, be entitled to the cash allow­
ances prescribed in subsection Al (b)  
hereof.
Section C. Quarterly Maintenance Al­
lowance.
1. The quarterly maintenance allow­
ance prescribed in section A hereof shall  
be payable on the first day of each quar­
ter to:
(a) Enlisted men entitled to a cloth­
ing allowance under subsections 1, 2, 3,  
4, 5, or 10 of section A, or subsections B5  
and B7 hereof, or who were entitled to a  
clothing allowance under Executive Or­
der 9356 of June 24, 1943, as amended,  
commencing with the first day of the  
quarter following the first anniversary  
of the date on which they were last en­
titled to such clothing allowance.
(b) Enlisted men of the Navy and  
Coast Guard reenlisting within three  
months from date of last discharge, en­
listed men of the Reserve components  
transferred to the regular Service, and  
enlisted men of the Regular and Reserve  
components on active duty transferred  
to the Reserve or to the Retired List and  
retained on active duty or recalled to ac­
tive duty within three months of release  
therefrom, at the rate applicable prior  
to such discharge, transfer, retirement,  
or release, until entitled to a further  
clothing allowance.
2. Enlisted men of the Naval Reserve  
undergoing training leading to a com­
mission, enlisted men of the Naval Re­
serve (inactive) and enlisted men hold­
ing temporary appointments to warrant  
or Commissioned rank shall not be en­
titled to quarterly maintenance allow­
ances. Enlisted men entitled to a  
clothing allowance on the first day of  
the quarter shall not be entitled to any  
quarterly maintenance allowance other­
wise due them on that date.
This order shall supersede Executive  
Orders No. 9744B of June 29, 1946, No.  
9785 of October 1, 1946, and No. 9869 of  
June 30, 1947, and shall be effective £ ls  
of July 1, 1948, and continue in effect  
for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949.

Section B. Clothing Allowance.
1. The amount of the cash clothing  
allowances prescribed in subsection Al  
(b) hereof shall be payable on date of  
first enlistment or first reporting for ac­
tive duty, and on date of reenlistment  
or recall to active duty subsequent to  
expiration of three months from date of  
last discharge or release from active duty,  
but shall not actually be paid prior to the
expiration of ninety days from and in­
cluding such date, or date of completion  
of recruit training, or date of advance­
ment to chief petty officer or assignment  
to band, whichever is earlier. In closing  
the accounts of a man discharged or re­
leased from active duty within the  
ninety-day period, credit shall be made  
only of an amount equal to the value of  
the clothing actually drawn, but in no  
case to exceed the total allowance pay­
able. ,
2. For the purposes of this order, an  
enlistment in any of the services men­
tioned in Section A subsequent to dis­
charge from any other of such services  
shall be considered a reenlistment. An  
allowance under subsection Al shall not  
be payable upon reenlistment within  
three months from date of last discharge,  
or upon recall to active duty within three  
months of last release therefrom, except  
as specified in subsections 5, 6 and 7 of  
this section. A man reenlisted or re­
called to active duty within three months  
of last discharge or release from active  
duty, who bn date of such discharge or  
release was checked undrawn clothing  
allowance in accordance with subsection  
P of this section, shall be entitled to  
credit for such undrawn clothing allow­
ance.
3. The allowance under subsection A2  
shall not be payable to—
(a) Enlisted men advanced in rating  
to chief petty officer while holding a tem­
porary appointment to warrant or com­
missioned rank.
(b> Cooks or stewards on advance­
ment to chief Gook or steward.
(c) Members of Navy, Naval Academy,  
or Coast Guard Academy Bands (band  
members) upon advancement in rating  
to chief petty officer.
4. An enlisted man reduced in rating  
from chief petty officer, cook, or steward  
shall not be required to refund payment  
previously made in accordance with sub­
section A2; and shall not be entitled to  
a second payment on subsequent ad-j  
vancement, or to a payment of quarterly  
maintenance allowance prior to the date  
specified in subsection Cl (a) hereof.
5. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A6 and A9 (b)  
hereof, upon subsequent transfer to,, or  
reenlistment within three months of last  
discharge in, another status which, in  
the case of first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a  
cash clothing allowance as prescribed in  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled to  
a credit of such cash clothing allowance  
without regard to issues in kind in the  
prior status, except that an enlisted man  
entitled to a clothing allowance under  
subsection A9 (b) on first reporting for  
active duty shall not be so entitled.
6. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A7 hereof,  
upon subsequent transfer to, or reenlist­
ment within three months of last dis­
charge in, another status which, in the  
case of a first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a
cash clothing allowance as prescribedjn  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled  
to a credit of such cash clothing allow­
ance without regard to issues in kind in  
the prior status..
7. Enlisted personnel described in sub­
section A9 (a), upon discharge from the  
Naval Reserve'(inactive) for the pur­
pose of enlisting in the Regular Navy or  
Coast Guard within three months from  
date of 'such discharge, shall, if reen­
listed in any of the applicable ratings,  
be entitled to a further cash allowance  
equal to the difference between the cash  
allowance payable under subsection Al  
(a) hereof, and the amount payable un­
der subsection A9 (a), and such enlisted  
personnel shall, if enlisted in other rat­
ings in the Regular Navy or Coast Guard, 
within three months from date of such  
discharge, be entitled to the cash allow­
ances prescribed in subsection Al (b)  
hereof.
Section C. Quarterly Maintenance Al­
lowance.
1. The quarterly maintenance allow­
ance prescribed in section A hereof shall  
be payable on the first day of each quar­
ter to:
(a) Enlisted men entitled to a cloth­
ing allowance under subsections 1, 2, 3,  
4, 5, or 10 of section A, or subsections B5  
and B7 hereof, or who were entitled to a  
clothing allowance under Executive Or­
der 9356 of June 24, 1943, as amended,  
commencing with the first day of the  
quarter following the first anniversary  
of the date on which they were last en­
titled to such clothing allowance.
(b) Enlisted men of the Navy and  
Coast Guard reenlisting within three  
months from date of last discharge, en­
listed men of the Reserve components  
transferred to the regular Service, and  
enlisted men of the Regular and Reserve  
components on active duty transferred  
to the Reserve or to the Retired List and  
retained on active duty or recalled to ac­
tive duty within three months of release  
therefrom, at the rate applicable prior  
to such discharge, transfer, retirement,  
or release, until entitled to a further  
clothing allowance.
2. Enlisted men of the Naval Reserve  
undergoing training leading to a com­
mission, enlisted men of the Naval Re­
serve (inactive) and enlisted men hold­
ing temporary appointments to warrant  
or Commissioned rank shall not be en­
titled to quarterly maintenance allow­
ances. Enlisted men entitled to a  
clothing allowance on the first day of  
the quarter shall not be entitled to any  
quarterly maintenance allowance other­
wise due them on that date.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The closing paragraph supersedes Executive Orders No. 9744B, No. 9785 and No. 9869, makes the order effective as of July 1, 1948 and provides that it shall “continue in effect for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949”. The supersession was performed on the effective date, July 1, 1948, and the effective-date statement was spent then; the duration command ends on June 30, 1949, so the clause as a whole ends on that date (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins). The end source is the order's own text.

August 4 as Coast Guard Day, in recog­
nition of the work of this agency of the  
Government, to the end that its 158th

observed with appropriate ceremonies.

other official flags be displayed on Coast

research_rationale:
Executive Order 9984 (13 FR 4437 (Federal Register of August 3, 1948)) was signed July 31, 1948. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. It prescribes regulations on clothing in kind or cash allowances in lieu of clothing for enlisted personnel of the Navy, Coast Guard, Naval Reserve and Coast Guard Reserve: Section A lists the allowances, Section B governs when the cash allowances are paid, Section C governs the quarterly maintenance allowance, and the closing paragraph supersedes Executive Order No. 9744B, No. 9785 and No. 9869, makes the order effective as of July 1, 1948 and provides that it shall “continue in effect for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949”. On 2026-10-14 every clause is terminated by that own-terms sunset, June 30, 1949. The dossier's forty clause fragments come from the OCR of the allowance tables and are replaced by five operative pieces: the lead, Sections A, B and C, and the closing paragraph. The searches for an earlier end found one later event, Executive Order 10023 (signed December 20, 1948, effective as of December 1, 1948), which adds subsection 11 to Section A and subsection 8 to Section B for members of the Navy Band; it is an amendment and not an end. A held-text search for citations of this order, with and without a trailing footnote digit, found only Executive Order 10023 and its copies and the Federal Register page of August 3, 1948. The Federal Register disposition-note search lists the one hit (Executive Order 10023); the U.S. Code and eCFR searches report no hit.

The end date recorded is June 30, 1949 on the inclusive reading, because the order continues for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1949; the exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is disclosed as the alternative.","independent_command_check":"No piece has an independent duration. Sections A to C operate together under the closing paragraph's single fiscal-year sunset.","savings_check":"The order's text has no saving clause. Allowances paid or accrued for enlisted service before the sunset are payments under the regulation; the held text creates no continuing duty after June 30, 1949, and the bounded searches found no later order continuing or restoring it.","scope_check":"Five operative pieces replace the dossier's forty fragments: the lead that prescribes the regulations; Section A (entitlements to clothing or cash allowances); Section B (when the cash allowances are payable, including conditions for reenlisted and transferred men); Section C (quarterly maintenance allowance); and the closing paragraph (supersession of three earlier orders, effective date, and duration). The closing paragraph's supersession of Executive Orders No. 9744B, No. 9785 and No. 9869 was performed when the order took effect on July 1, 1948 and is disclosed as exhausted then, but the paragraph also carries the duration, so the clause as a whole ends with the sunset."}

savings_residuals.reason: The order's text has no saving clause. Allowances paid or accrued for enlisted service before the sunset are payments under the regulation; the held text creates no continuing duty after June 30, 1949, and the bounded searches found no later order continuing or restoring it.

August 4 as Coast Guard Day, in recog­
nition of the work of this agency of the

Section B. Clothing Allowance.
1. The amount of the cash clothing  
allowances prescribed in subsection Al  
(b) hereof shall be payable on date of  
first enlistment or first reporting for ac­
tive duty, and on date of reenlistment  
or recall to active duty subsequent to  
expiration of three months from date of  
last discharge or release from active duty,  
but shall not actually be paid prior to the
expiration of ninety days from and in­
cluding such date, or date of completion  
of recruit training, or date of advance­
ment to chief petty officer or assignment  
to band, whichever is earlier. In closing  
the accounts of a man discharged or re­
leased from active duty within the  
ninety-day period, credit shall be made  
only of an amount equal to the value of  
the clothing actually drawn, but in no  
case to exceed the total allowance pay­
able. ,
2. For the purposes of this order, an  
enlistment in any of the services men­
tioned in Section A subsequent to dis­
charge from any other of such services  
shall be considered a reenlistment. An  
allowance under subsection Al shall not  
be payable upon reenlistment within  
three months from date of last discharge,  
or upon recall to active duty within three  
months of last release therefrom, except  
as specified in subsections 5, 6 and 7 of  
this section. A man reenlisted or re­
called to active duty within three months  
of last discharge or release from active  
duty, who bn date of such discharge or  
release was checked undrawn clothing  
allowance in accordance with subsection  
P of this section, shall be entitled to  
credit for such undrawn clothing allow­
ance.
3. The allowance under subsection A2  
shall not be payable to—
(a) Enlisted men advanced in rating  
to chief petty officer while holding a tem­
porary appointment to warrant or com­
missioned rank.
(b> Cooks or stewards on advance­
ment to chief Gook or steward.
(c) Members of Navy, Naval Academy,  
or Coast Guard Academy Bands (band  
members) upon advancement in rating  
to chief petty officer.

from chief petty officer, cook, or steward  
shall not be required to refund payment

section A2; and shall not be entitled to  
a second payment on subsequent ad-j  
vancement, or to a payment of quarterly  
maintenance allowance prior to the date  
specified in subsection Cl (a) hereof.
5. An enlisted man first reporting for  
active duty in a status entitling him  
only to an issue of clothing in kind in ac­
cordance with subsection A6 and A9 (b)  
hereof, upon subsequent transfer to,, or  
reenlistment within three months of last  
discharge in, another status which, in

cordance with subsection A7 hereof,  
upon subsequent transfer to, or reenlist­
ment within three months of last dis­

case of a first enlistment or reporting  
for active duty, would entitle him to a
cash clothing allowance as prescribedjn  
subsection Al hereof, shall be entitled  
to a credit of such cash clothing allow­
ance without regard to issues in kind in

section A9 (a), upon discharge from the  
Naval Reserve'(inactive) for the pur­
pose of enlisting in the Regular Navy or

date of 'such discharge, shall, if reen­

ings in the Regular Navy or Coast Guard,

Section C. Quarterly Maintenance Al­
lowance.
1. The quarterly maintenance allow­
ance prescribed in section A hereof shall  
be payable on the first day of each quar­
ter to:
(a) Enlisted men entitled to a cloth­
ing allowance under subsections 1, 2, 3,

titled to such clothing allowance.
(b) Enlisted men of the Navy and  
Coast Guard reenlisting within three  
months from date of last discharge, en­
listed men of the Reserve components  
transferred to the regular Service, and  
enlisted men of the Regular and Reserve  
components on active duty transferred  
to the Reserve or to the Retired List and  
retained on active duty or recalled to ac­
tive duty within three months of release  
therefrom, at the rate applicable prior  
to such discharge, transfer, retirement,  
or release, until entitled to a further  
clothing allowance.
2. Enlisted men of the Naval Reserve  
undergoing training leading to a com­
mission, enlisted men of the Naval Re­
serve (inactive) and enlisted men hold­

the quarter shall not be entitled to any

wise due them on that date.

Washington, Saturday ,  December 4, 1948
TITLE 3— THE PRESIDENT
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10019
Excusing F ederal Employees  From D uty 
One-H alf Day on December 24,1948
By virtue of the authority vested in me  
as President of the United States, it is  
hereby ordered that the several executive  
departments, independent establish­
ments, and other governmental agencies  
in the metropolitan area of the District  
of Columbia, including the General Ac­
counting Office, the Government Printing 
Office, and the Navy Yard and Naval Sta­
tions, shall be closed one-half day on  
Friday, December 24, 1948, the day pre­
ceding Christmas Day; and all employees  
in the Federal service in the metropolitan  
area of the District of Columbia, and in  
the field service of the executive depart­
ments, independent establishments, and  
other agencies of the Government, except  
those who may for special public reasons  
be excluded from the provisions of this  
order by the heads of their respective  
departments, establishments, or agencies, 
or those whose absence from duty would  
be inconsistent with the provisions of ex­
isting law, shall be excused from duty for  
one-half day on December 24,1948.
H arry S. T ruman
The White  H ouse,
December 2,1948.
[P. R. Doc. 48-10659; Piled, Dec. 8, 1948;
11:11 a. m.]

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sole paragraph closes the offices “shall be closed one-half day on Friday, December 24, 1948” and excuses employees “shall be excused from duty for one-half day on December 24,1948”. Both commands are limited to December 24, 1948, so the clause ended on that day by its own terms. The date is recorded inclusive (the order runs through the end of December 24, 1948); the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. The end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10019 (13 FR 7395 (Federal Register of December 4, 1948)) was signed December 2, 1948. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. Its only paragraph orders that the executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies in the District of Columbia metropolitan area “shall be closed one-half day on Friday, December 24, 1948”, and that employees in the metropolitan area and in the field service, except those excluded by agency heads for special public reasons or whose absence would be inconsistent with existing law, “shall be excused from duty for one-half day on December 24,1948”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated by its own terms: it applies to the single named day, December 24, 1948, and has no operation after that day. The order contains no other command, no condition and no continuing duty. A search of the held texts for the order's number found only the order's own Federal Register page. The Federal Register disposition-note, U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit naming this order.

The order creates no continuing duty.","savings_check":"Nothing survives the day: the order excused employees from duty for a half day, grants no continuing leave or pay right beyond that half day, and has no saving clause. The bounded searches found no later instrument that continues or restores it.","scope_check":"The order has one operative paragraph containing two related commands, the closing of offices for one-half day and the excusing of employees for the same half day, both tied to December 24, 1948. The inventory has no other clause."}

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10068 (14 FR 3883 (Federal Register of July 14, 1949)) was signed July 13, 1949. The filing stamp printed after the order reads July 13, 1949. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence providing that Executive Order No. 2458 of September 20, 1916 “is hereby revoked”. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on July 13, 1949. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. No other held text cites this order's number by an order citation, so there is no later recital, amendment or restoration of it in the held corpus. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 2458 of September 20, 1916, which established the Inter-Departmental Board on International Service of Ice Observation, Ice Patrol, and Ocean Derelict Destruction remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists, because the only command in the order is the revocation itself and it was performed when the order took effect on July 13, 1949. The order states no effective date other than signing. The filing stamp printed after the order reads July 13, 1949. If the revocation were instead read as effective only on that filing, the date would be later than the date recorded here; the order text itself supplies no such rule. No later instrument is claimed as an end.","independent_command_check":"The only command is the revocation. The order creates no independent continuing duty, board, fund or authority that could outlast it; whatever the revoked instrument itself provided is outside this order and is not claimed here.","savings_check":"The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Order No. 2458 of September 20, 1916, which established the Inter-Departmental Board on International Service of Ice Observation, Ice Patrol, and Ocean Derelict Destruction stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked.","scope_check":"The held text has the operative inventory stated in the clause rows and no other command: no standstill, report, appointment, transfer or savings sentence."}

§  643.133 Maturity and satisfaction —
(a) Loans. Loans mature on demand 
but not later than January 31, 1950, for 
Arizona, California and Texas, and not 
later than April 30, 1950, for all other 
States. In the case of farm storage 
loans, the producer is required to pay 
off his loan on or before maturity, or to 
deliver the mortgaged flaxseed in ac­
cordance with instructions of the county 
committee. Credit will be given at the 
applicable loan value, according to grade 
and/or quality for the total quantity 
delivered, provided it was stored in the 
bin(s) in which the flaxseed under loan 
was stored. The loan value (county loan 
rates), for flaxseed delivered to CCC un­
der a farm storage loan will be set forth 
in this bulletin and in supplements or 
amendments thereto.
If the settlement value of the flaxseed 
delivered under a farm storage loan ex­
ceeds the amount due under the loan, 
the amount of the excess shall be paid 
to the producer by a sight draft drawn 
on CCC by the State PMA office.
If the settlement value of the flaxseed 
is less than the amount due on the loan, 
the amount of the deficiency, plus Inter­
est, shall be paid by the producer to 
CCC, or may be set off against any pay­
ment which would otherwise be made 
to the producer under any agricultural 
program administered by the Secretary 
of Agriculture, or any other payments 
which are due or may become due to the 
producer from CCC or any other agency 
of the United States. In the event the 
farm is sold or there is a change of ten­
ancy, the flaxseed may be delivered be­
fore the maturity date of the loan, upon 
prior approval by the county committee.
In the case of warehouse storage loans, 
if the producer does not repay his loan 
by maturity, CCC shall have the right 
to sell or pool the flaxseed in satisfaction 
of the loan In accordance with the pro­
visions of the note and loan agreement 
and §  643.134. Any payment due a pro­
ducer at the time of settlement on a 
warehouse storage loan, shall be made 
by the appropriate PMA commodity 
office.

The command was exhausted by performance and the end source is the order's own text.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10093 (14 FR 7681 (Federal Register of December 23, 1949)) was signed December 20, 1949. The filing stamp printed after the order reads December 22, 1949, two days after signing. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence providing that Executive Order No. 9512 of January 16, 1945 “is hereby revoked”. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on December 20, 1949. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. The only other held text containing this order's number is the Federal Register page that reproduces this same order (EO_10092.txt, issue of December 23, 1949); it is the same instrument, not a later one. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9512 of January 16, 1945, which provided for coordination of the allocations of field positions subject to the Classification Act of 1923, as amended remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists, because the only command in the order is the revocation itself and it was performed when the order took effect on December 20, 1949. The order states no effective date other than signing. The filing stamp printed after the order reads December 22, 1949, two days after signing. If the revocation were instead read as effective only on that filing, the date would be later than the date recorded here; the order text itself supplies no such rule. No later instrument is claimed as an end.","independent_command_check":"The only command is the revocation. The order creates no independent continuing duty, board, fund or authority that could outlast it; whatever the revoked instrument itself provided is outside this order and is not claimed here.","savings_check":"The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Order No. 9512 of January 16, 1945, which provided for coordination of the allocations of field positions subject to the Classification Act of 1923, as amended stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked.","scope_check":"The held text has the operative inventory stated in the clause rows and no other command: no standstill, report, appointment, transfer or savings sentence."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order's single sentence provides that Executive Order No. 8232 of September 5, 1939 “be, and it is hereby, revoked”. It states no effective date, so the revocation took effect when signed on February 8, 1950; the filing stamp reads February 8, 1950 as well. The command was exhausted by performance on that date and the end source is the order's own text. The Agriculture Department notice that follows on the page is not part of the order.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10107 (15 FR 701 (Federal Register of February 9, 1950)) was signed February 8, 1950. The filing stamp printed after the order reads February 8, 1950. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence ordering that Executive Order No. 8232 of September 5, 1939 “be, and it is hereby, revoked”. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on February 8, 1950. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. No other held text cites this order's number by an order citation. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 8232 of September 5, 1939, entitled “Control of the Panama Canal and the Canal Zone” remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end exists, because the only command in the order is the revocation itself and it was performed when the order took effect on February 8, 1950. The order states no effective date other than signing. The filing stamp printed after the order reads February 8, 1950. If the revocation were instead read as effective only on that filing, the date would be later than the date recorded here; the order text itself supplies no such rule. No later instrument is claimed as an end.","independent_command_check":"The only command is the revocation. The order creates no independent continuing duty, board, fund or authority that could outlast it; whatever the revoked instrument itself provided is outside this order and is not claimed here.","savings_check":"The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Order No. 8232 of September 5, 1939, entitled “Control of the Panama Canal and the Canal Zone” stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked.","scope_check":"The held text has the operative inventory stated in the clause rows and no other command: no standstill, report, appointment, transfer or savings sentence. The dossier's inventory ran the clause through an unrelated Department of Agriculture termination notice printed on the same Federal Register page; the inventory is corrected to the order's single sentence only."}

savings_residuals.reason: The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Order No. 8232 of September 5, 1939, entitled “Control of the Panama Canal and the Canal Zone” stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked.

FEDERAL REGISTER 2265Saturday, A pril 22, 1950
EXECUTIVE ORDER 10123
R evocation of E xecutive O rders N o. 
96351  of S eptember 29, 1945, and N o. 
99041  of N ovember 13, 1947
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
as President of the United States, it is 
ordered as follows:
Executive Order No. 9635 of September 
29, 1945, relating to the organization of
the Navy Department and the Naval 
Establishment, and Executive Order No. 
9904 of November 13,1947, amending the 
said Executive Order No. 9635, are hereby 
revoked.
The revocation made by this order 
shall not be construed as reviving Execu­
tive Order No, 8984 of December 18,1941, 
and Executive ¿Order No. 9096 of March
12, 1942 (as amended by Executive 
Order No. 9528 of March 2, 1945), re­
voked by the said Executive Order No. 
9635.
Harry S. T ruman
The W hite H ouse,
April 2d, 1950.
[P. R. Doc. 50-3445; Piled, Apr. 20, 1950;  
4:45 p. m.]
RULES AND REGULATIONS
TITLE 14— CIVIL AVIATION
Chapter II—-Civil Aeronautics Admin­
istration, Department of Commerce
Part 575—F ederal Civil Airports on 
Canton and W ake I slands
Under section 10 (a) of the Interna­
tional Aviation Facilities Act, the Ad­
ministrator of Civil ‘ Aeronautics is 
empowered and directed to do and per­
form all acts and things necessary or 
incident to the operation, protection, 
maintenance, improvement, and admin­
istration of airport property in territory 
outside the continental limits of the 
United States which he has acquired pur­
suant to the act or any other provision of 
law. This includes the power to make 
and amend such reasonable rules and 
regulations as he may deem necessary 
to the proper exercise of the powers 
granted by the section, and to make just 
and reasonable charges for aeronautical 
services, including but not limited to 
landing f66S.
Acting pursuant to the foregoing au­
thority, and in accordance with section 
3 (a) (3) of the Administrative Pro­
cedure Act, Part 575 is hereby adopted. 
The charges contained in this Part have 
been established at a level which is con­
sidered to be Within the ability of civil 
aviation to pay, and will be only partially 
compensatory at this time for the costs 
to the United States Government of 
maintaining and operating the landing 
areas involved. As ability of civil avia­
tion to pay changes, the level of charges 
will be revised with a view to recovering, 
as soon as practicable, the total costs of 
maintaining and operating the- landing 
areas.
SUBPABT A— INTRODUCTION
Sec. >
575.1 Explanation of terms.
SUBPART B— LANDING AND PARKING FEES
575.11 Landing fees.
575.12 Parking fees.
675.13 Alteration of fees.
575.14 Payment of fees.
SUBPART C— LOADING AND UNLOADING AREAS
575.21 Control of areas.
A u t h o r i t y: §§ 575.1 through 575.21 Issued  
under sec. 10, 62 Stat. 453; 49 U. S. C. Sup.,  
4159.
SUBPART A — INTRODUCTION
§  575.1 Explanation of terms —(a) 
Aircraft weight.  “Aircraft weight” shall 
mean the maximum take-off weight per­
mitted by the appropriate aeronautical 
authority of the State of manufacture
13 CFR, 1945 Supp.; i0 F. R. 12419.  
* •3  CFR, 1947 Supp.; 12 F. R. 7613.
of the aircraft. It shall be calculated to 
the nearest 1,000 pounds.
(b) Airport. “Airport” shall mean 
the Canton Island airport and the Wake 
Island airport operated by the Civil Aero­
nautics "  Administration.
(c) CAA. “CAA” shall mean the Civil 
Aeronautics Administration.
SUBPART B — LANDING AND PARKING FEES
§  575.11 Landing fees— t a) Rate of  
charge. A charge of 16 cents per 1,000 
pounds shall be made for each landing 
of an aircraft at the airport. (No addi­
tional charge .for each take-off shall be 
made.)(b) Exceptions to charge.  The follow­
ing aircraft shall not be subject to land­
ing fees:(1) Civil aircraft not engaged in com­
mercial operations;
(2) Aircraft engaged in test flights. 
(This shall not include survey and 
proving runs);
(3) Aircraft compelled to return after 
take-off;-
(4) Public aircraft not engaged in 
commercial operations.
§  575.12 Parking fees— (a) Hangar 
parking fee.  A charge of 5 cents per 
1,000 pounds of aircraft weight shall be 
made for each 6-hour period or fraction 
thereof during which an aircraft is 
parked in a hangar at the airport.
(b) Outside parking fee.  A charge of 
2.5 cents per 1,000 pounds of aircraft 
weight shall be made for each 6-hour 
period or fraction thereof during which 
an aircraft is parked outside at the air­
port. The charge shall start six hours 
after the plane lands.
§  575.13 Alteration of fees.  Charges 
for-aircraft based at the airport may be 
fixed by the CAA Regional Administrator 
having jurisdiction over the airport, 
without regard to the landing and park­
ing fees provided in §§ 575.11 and 575.12.
§  575.14 Payment of fees —(a) Time 
and means of payment.  Fees shall be 
paid in United States dollars at the time 
use is made of the airport.
(b) Exceptions to time of payment.  
Scheduled air carriers and other aircraft 
operators may make prior financial ar­
rangements with the CAA official in 
charge of the airport. These arrange­
ments may include provision for pay­
ment on a monthly or other suitable 
basis.
SUBPART C — LOADING AND UNLOADING A REAS
§  575.21 Control of areas.  The CAA 
official in charge of the airport shall have 
full control of the loading and unloading 
areas to insure efficient and noh-discrim-
inatory utilization. Such authority shall 
inplude, but shall not necessarily be lim­
ited to, the right to:
(a) Assign space and sequence of use 
when lie-concludes that it is necessary 
or advisable;
(b) Order the movement of a stand­
ing aircraft to conform with assign­
ments under paragraph (a) of this 
sêction ;
(c) Assess an excess parking fee of 
$5 per hour for non-conformity with 
paragraph (b) of this section.
This part shall become effective May 1, 
1950.
[seal] D onald W. N yrop,
Acting Administrator of  
Civil Aeronautics.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The second sentence says the revocation made by this order shall not be construed as reviving Executive Order No. 8984 and Executive Order No. 9096 (as amended), which Executive Order No. 9635 had revoked. It limits only the effect of the revocation performed in the first sentence, so it operated once, when that revocation took effect on April 20, 1950, and has no separate continuing command. Its consequence, that the two named earlier orders were not revived, is disclosed as a surviving effect and is not claimed as an operative command.

Executive Order 10123 (15 FR 2265 (Federal Register of April 22, 1950)) was signed April 20, 1950. The filing stamp printed after the order reads April 20, 1950; the held OCR prints the signing line as April 2d, 1950, which is the register's signing date of April 20, 1950 read through an OCR error. Its held Federal Register text, registered as the original representation for this order, prints the order number, its title and the signing date, and its operative command is the sentence providing that Executive Order No. 9635 and Executive Order No. 9904, which amended it, “are hereby revoked”, followed by a sentence limiting the effect of the revocation. On 2026-10-14 the command is terminated: a revoking command is complete when it takes effect, and this order states no separate effective date, so it took effect when signed on April 20, 1950. The order contains no condition, postponement, report, transfer or continuing duty. No other held text cites this order's number by an order citation. The Federal Register disposition-note search, the U.S. Code citation search and the eCFR citation search each report no hit naming this order; the last two test only for current citations and are cited as bounded searches. The surviving consequence is that Executive Order No. 9635 of September 29, 1945 (organization of the Navy Department and the Naval Establishment) and Executive Order No. 9904 of November 13, 1947, which amended it remains revoked; that consequence follows from the performed command and is not a command that still has to end.

If the revocation were instead read as effective only on that filing, the date would be later than the date recorded here; the order text itself supplies no such rule. The order's second sentence says the revocation is not to be construed as reviving Executive Order No. 8984 and Executive Order No. 9096 (as amended), which Executive Order No. 9635 had revoked; those two orders therefore stay revoked.","scope_check":"The held text has the operative inventory stated in the clause rows and no other command: no standstill, report, appointment, transfer or savings sentence. savings_residuals.reason: The revocation is a performed act whose consequence (Executive Order No. 9635 of September 29, 1945 (organization of the Navy Department and the Naval Establishment) and Executive Order No. 9904 of November 13, 1947, which amended it stays revoked) survives; the held text contains no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later order that restores or continues what was revoked. The order's second sentence says the revocation is not to be construed as reviving Executive Order No. 8984 and Executive Order No. 9096 (as amended), which Executive Order No. 9635 had revoked; those two orders therefore stay revoked.

RULES AND REGULATIONS
TITLE 14— CIVIL AVIATION
Chapter II—-Civil Aeronautics Admin­
istration, Department of Commerce
Part 575—F ederal Civil Airports on 
Canton and W ake I slands
Under section 10 (a) of the Interna­
tional Aviation Facilities Act, the Ad­
ministrator of Civil ‘ Aeronautics is 
empowered and directed to do and per­
form all acts and things necessary or 
incident to the operation, protection, 
maintenance, improvement, and admin­
istration of airport property in territory 
outside the continental limits of the 
United States which he has acquired pur­
suant to the act or any other provision of 
law. This includes the power to make 
and amend such reasonable rules and 
regulations as he may deem necessary 
to the proper exercise of the powers 
granted by the section, and to make just 
and reasonable charges for aeronautical 
services, including but not limited to 
landing f66S.
Acting pursuant to the foregoing au­
thority, and in accordance with section 
3 (a) (3) of the Administrative Pro­
cedure Act, Part 575 is hereby adopted. 
The charges contained in this Part have 
been established at a level which is con­
sidered to be Within the ability of civil 
aviation to pay, and will be only partially 
compensatory at this time for the costs 
to the United States Government of 
maintaining and operating the landing 
areas involved. As ability of civil avia­
tion to pay changes, the level of charges 
will be revised with a view to recovering, 
as soon as practicable, the total costs of 
maintaining and operating the- landing 
areas.
SUBPABT A— INTRODUCTION
Sec. >
575.1 Explanation of terms.
SUBPART B— LANDING AND PARKING FEES
575.11 Landing fees.
575.12 Parking fees.
675.13 Alteration of fees.
575.14 Payment of fees.
SUBPART C— LOADING AND UNLOADING AREAS
575.21 Control of areas.
A u t h o r i t y: §§ 575.1 through 575.21 Issued  
under sec. 10, 62 Stat. 453; 49 U. S. C. Sup.,  
4159.
SUBPART A — INTRODUCTION
§  575.1 Explanation of terms —(a) 
Aircraft weight.  “Aircraft weight” shall 
mean the maximum take-off weight per­
mitted by the appropriate aeronautical 
authority of the State of manufacture
13 CFR, 1945 Supp.; i0 F. R. 12419.  
* •3  CFR, 1947 Supp.; 12 F. R. 7613.
of the aircraft. It shall be calculated to 
the nearest 1,000 pounds.
(b) Airport. “Airport” shall mean 
the Canton Island airport and the Wake 
Island airport operated by the Civil Aero­
nautics "  Administration.
(c) CAA. “CAA” shall mean the Civil 
Aeronautics Administration.
SUBPART B — LANDING AND PARKING FEES
§  575.11 Landing fees— t a) Rate of  
charge. A charge of 16 cents per 1,000 
pounds shall be made for each landing 
of an aircraft at the airport. (No addi­
tional charge .for each take-off shall be 
made.)(b) Exceptions to charge.  The follow­
ing aircraft shall not be subject to land­
ing fees:(1) Civil aircraft not engaged in com­
mercial operations;
(2) Aircraft engaged in test flights. 
(This shall not include survey and 
proving runs);
(3) Aircraft compelled to return after 
take-off;-
(4) Public aircraft not engaged in 
commercial operations.
§  575.12 Parking fees— (a) Hangar 
parking fee.  A charge of 5 cents per 
1,000 pounds of aircraft weight shall be 
made for each 6-hour period or fraction 
thereof during which an aircraft is 
parked in a hangar at the airport.
(b) Outside parking fee.  A charge of 
2.5 cents per 1,000 pounds of aircraft 
weight shall be made for each 6-hour 
period or fraction thereof during which 
an aircraft is parked outside at the air­
port. The charge shall start six hours 
after the plane lands.
§  575.13 Alteration of fees.  Charges 
for-aircraft based at the airport may be 
fixed by the CAA Regional Administrator 
having jurisdiction over the airport, 
without regard to the landing and park­
ing fees provided in §§ 575.11 and 575.12.
§  575.14 Payment of fees —(a) Time 
and means of payment.  Fees shall be 
paid in United States dollars at the time 
use is made of the airport.
(b) Exceptions to time of payment.  
Scheduled air carriers and other aircraft 
operators may make prior financial ar­
rangements with the CAA official in 
charge of the airport. These arrange­
ments may include provision for pay­
ment on a monthly or other suitable 
basis.
SUBPART C — LOADING AND UNLOADING A REAS
§  575.21 Control of areas.  The CAA 
official in charge of the airport shall have 
full control of the loading and unloading 
areas to insure efficient and noh-discrim-
inatory utilization. Such authority shall 
inplude, but shall not necessarily be lim­
ited to, the right to:
(a) Assign space and sequence of use 
when lie-concludes that it is necessary 
or advisable;
(b) Order the movement of a stand­
ing aircraft to conform with assign­
ments under paragraph (a) of this 
sêction ;
(c) Assess an excess parking fee of 
$5 per hour for non-conformity with 
paragraph (b) of this section.
This part shall become effective May 1, 
1950.
[seal] D onald W. N yrop,
Acting Administrator of  
Civil Aeronautics.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10129 (15 FR 3499 (Federal Register of June 6, 1950)) was signed June 3, 1950. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date; the text breaks across a page after paragraph 7 and resumes on a later page of the same issue, so paragraph 7 appears in two pieces. It creates the President's Commission on Migratory Labor (paragraph 1), directs it to inquire into five subjects (paragraph 2), requires a written report by December 15, 1950 (paragraph 3), authorizes hearings (paragraph 4), directs consultation with the Department of State (paragraph 5), directs agency cooperation (paragraph 6), provides funding for the fiscal years 1950 and 1951 from the Emergency Fund for the President (paragraph 7) and provides in paragraph 8 that the Commission ceases to exist thirty days after its report unless otherwise determined by further Executive Order. On 2026-10-14 every clause is terminated on May 31, 1951, the day the Commission ceased to exist. Executive Order 10192 (15 FR 9029 (Federal Register of December 19, 1950)), signed December 15, 1950, amended paragraph 3 (the report date becomes March 1, 1951) and paragraph 8 (“Thirty days” becomes “Sixty days”). Executive Order 10236 (16 FR 3607 (Federal Register of April 27, 1951)), signed April 26, 1951, amended paragraph 8 as amended to read “The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31,1951.”, which fixes the end. The report date of paragraph 3 and the report-relative cessation of paragraph 8 are not ends: the held corpus does not give the date the report was rendered, and Executive Order 10236 replaced the report-relative rule with a fixed date while the Commission still existed. Executive Order 10193's Federal Register page contains the text of Executive Order 10192 and cites Executive Order 10129 only for that reason; it is not a separate amendment. The held-text search for citations of the order found only Executive Orders 10192, 10236 and their page copies. The Federal Register disposition-note search lists two hits (the 10192 and 10236 amendments); the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit.

The only rule that could have ended the Commission earlier is paragraph 8's original report-relative cessation (thirty days, then sixty days, after the report was rendered). The held corpus does not state when the report was rendered, but Executive Order 10236 of April 26, 1951 amended paragraph 8 to a fixed date and treats the Commission as continuing to May 31, 1951; had the report-relative period already run, there would have been nothing left to amend. The date recorded is May 31, 1951; Executive Order 10236 says the Commission ceases “at the end of” that day, so the inclusive and exclusive readings coincide with the close of May 31, 1951. dent.

cational conditions among migratory

and

law enforcement measures and the au­

strengthened and improved to eliminate

port of its studies to the President in

ernmental action, either legislative or
