Adopted by the Civil Aeronautics 
Board at its office in Washington, D. C., 
on the 13th day of February 1951.
Under current regulations applicants 
for commercial pilot certificates are re­
quired to meet the second-class physical 
standards. Such standards include a 
requirement for “normal fields of vision” 
which has been interpreted to require 
those applicants to have normal color 
vision. Under current requirements 
student and private pilots who are re­
quired to meet third-class physical 
standards have not had to demonstrate 
normal color vision. An amendment of 
Part 29, being adopted concurrently with 
this amendment, changes the color vi­
sion requirement for the second-class 
physical standard to make it more di­
rectly related to aviation safety, and for
the first time adds a color vision require­
ment to the third-class physical stand­
ards. The amendments provide that 
applicants for all pilot certificates shall 
have the ability to distinguish aviation 
signal red, aviatron signal green, and 
white. (See the amendment of Part 29 
for details with respect to the changed 
requirements and the manner of ad­
ministration thereof.) This amendment 
of Part 20 provides that an applicant 
who is unable to distinguish these avia­
tion signal colors may still be issued a 
pilot certificate, restricted, however, to 
the exercise of the certificate privileges 
under such conditions, or with the use of 
such equipment, as will not require the 
ability to distinguish aviation signal 
colors.
Interested persons have been afforded 
an opportunity to participate in the 
making of this amendment, and due con­
sideration has been given to all relevant 
matter presented.
In consideration of the foregoing the 
Civil Aeronautics Board hereby amends 
Part 20 of the Civil Air Regulations (14 
CFR Part 20 as amended) effective 
March 20, 1951.

follows:
§  20.5 Physical standards —(a) Pow­
ered aircraft.  Applicant shall meet the

ability to distinguish such aviation signal

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sentence exempts Arthur A. Quinn from compulsory retirement for age “for an indefinite period of time, not extending beyond June 30, 1951”. The order fixes no earlier end event, so the stated date is the latest date the exemption could last and is the best supported end date. It is recorded inclusive (through June 30, 1951); the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. An earlier lapse, such as separation from office, is not shown by any held source and is disclosed as unestablished.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10215 (16 FR 1703 (Federal Register of February 20, 1951)) was signed February 16, 1951. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. Its only operative command exempts Arthur A. Quinn, Comptroller of Customs with headquarters at New York, New York, from compulsory retirement for age under the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, “for an indefinite period of time, not extending beyond June 30, 1951”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated: by its own words the exemption cannot extend beyond June 30, 1951. The period is described as indefinite but capped, so the cap is the latest date on which the exemption could be in force. No held source shows that the exemption lapsed earlier (for example by Mr. Quinn's separation from office), and none shows any extension: the person-name search of the held order texts found no other order naming him, and the held-text search for the order's number found no citation. The Federal Register disposition-note, U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit naming this order. The best supported date is therefore June 30, 1951, recorded on the inclusive reading, with the possibility of an earlier factual lapse disclosed. The dossier split the sentence into a long fragment and the five-character fragment “1951.”; the inventory is corrected to the single operative sentence.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The only end the held evidence supports is the order's own cap. An exemption of this kind could also become moot if the person left office earlier, but no held text records a separation, a death, a successor or a further exemption, and the owner ruling on evidence permits an interval or date only when evidence shows the event in it; the cap is shown by the order's own text. The date recorded is June 30, 1951 on the inclusive reading, under which the exemption runs through that day; the exclusive reading, under which it ends when June 30 begins, is the alternative.","independent_command_check":"The order has a single command with a single cap; it contains no separate continuing duty.","savings_check":"The exemption only allows continued service despite reaching retirement age; the order creates no right that outlives the cap, has no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no later instrument continuing it.","scope_check":"One operative sentence (the exemption); the recital that the public interest requires it is not a command. The dossier's two fragments are merged into one clause."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The sentence exempts Bernice Pyke from compulsory retirement for age, effective as of April 1, 1950, “for an indefinite period of time not extending beyond March 31, 1952, the date on which her present term of office expires”. The cap is the order's own end and equals the date her present term expires, so it is recorded as the end, inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when March 31, 1952 begins. Executive Order 10333 of March 25, 1952 further exempts her for a new indefinite period “not extending beyond the appointment and qualification of her successor”; that is a later extension with its own term and is not treated as an end of this order.

lic interest requires that Bernice Pyke, 
Collector of Customs for Customs Col­
lection District No. 41, with headquarters 
at Cleveland, Ohio, be exempted from 
compulsory retirement for age as pro­
vided below:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 204 of 
the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 404 (5

Pyke be, and she is hereby, exempted 
from compulsory retirement for age 
under the provisions of the Civil Service

amended, for an indefinite period of time 
not extending beyond March 31, 1952, 
the date on which her present term of 
office expires.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10225 (16 FR 2544 (Federal Register of March 20, 1951)) was signed March 17, 1951. Its held Federal Register text prints the order number, the title and the signing date. Its only operative command exempts Bernice Pyke, Collector of Customs for Customs Collection District No. 41 with headquarters at Cleveland, Ohio, from compulsory retirement for age under the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended, effective as of April 1, 1950 (the order was signed nearly a year after that date), “for an indefinite period of time not extending beyond March 31, 1952, the date on which her present term of office expires”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated by its own terms on March 31, 1952, the date on which her present term of office expires. Executive Order 10333 (17 FR 2705 (Federal Register of March 28, 1952)), signed March 25, 1952, recites this order, says that she was exempted by it for an indefinite period of time not extending beyond March 31, 1952, and further exempts her for an indefinite period “not extending beyond the appointment and qualification of her successor”. That is a later extension by a new order with its own term, recorded as a later event and not as the end of this order; it also shows that the exemption had not lapsed before March 25, 1952. The person-name search found Executive Order 10333 and the neighbouring Federal Register page that also prints this order (Executive Order 10224 on the same page); no other held text names her. The Federal Register disposition-note, U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit naming this order.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end is shown. The exemption's own cap, March 31, 1952, is the end; Executive Order 10333, signed March 25, 1952, treats the exemption as still in place six days before the cap and extends it for a new term. The date recorded is March 31, 1952 on the inclusive reading (the exemption runs through that day); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative. A later further exemption is a later event with its own date and quotation, not this order's end.","independent_command_check":"The order has a single command with a single cap and no separate continuing duty. Executive Order 10333 creates a new exemption that is not part of this order.","savings_check":"The exemption only allows continued service despite reaching retirement age; the order creates no right that outlives March 31, 1952, has no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no instrument continuing this exemption other than the separate further exemption in Executive Order 10333.","scope_check":"One operative sentence (the exemption, made effective as of April 1, 1950). The recital that the public interest requires it is not a command."}

savings_residuals.reason: The exemption only allows continued service despite reaching retirement age; the order creates no right that outlives March 31, 1952, has no saving clause, and the bounded searches found no instrument continuing this exemption other than the separate further exemption in Executive Order 10333.

Exemption op B ernice P yke F rom C om­
pulsory R etirement for A ge
WHEREAS, in my judgment, the pub­
lic interest requires that Bernice Pyke, 
Collector of Customs for Customs Col­
lection District No. 41, with headquarters 
at Cleveland, Ohio, be exempted from 
compulsory retirement for age as pro­
vided below:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 204 of 
the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 404 (5 
U. S. C. 715a), it is ordered, effective as 
of April 1, 1950, that the said Bernice 
Pyke be, and she is hereby, exempted 
from compulsory retirement for age 
under the provisions of the Civil Service 
Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as 
amended, for an indefinite period of time 
not extending beyond March 31, 1952, 
the date on which her present term of 
office expires.
Harry S. T ruman
The W hite H ouse,
